title: Per-new-frame cost of the hybrid path versus full-GPU fine4
question: Round 40 compared formal calls that reuse one unchanged source: the hybrid Session reuses the pose context built by its first call, the complete GPU path rebuilds all source-dependent state every call. Which method is faster when every call receives a new frame through Session::updateSource, at many128_pose and many512_pose, with the six-object and 8K controls?
replaces: The archive-only estimate in GPU_NCC_CLOSURE_zh-TW.md section 2026-10-19 (hybrid formal median plus the median first-call pose_create_ms; marked NOT RUN for a real per-new-frame measurement).

source.compiled_source_changes_since_build_head: none; the frozen commit only adds cpp-core/tools/benchmark_new_frame_cost.py and cpp-core/tests/test_new_frame_cost_harness.py
source.snapshot: source-snapshot.tar.gz (286 committed files, stage-40 selection rule) and source-sha256.json

build.pre_measurement_validation: ctest 73/73, Python harness 567/567, color_verify_runner_test --metal 5/5, all before any timing

inputs.fixtures_manifest: stage-37 formal manifest; every source/template SHA256 checked against it
inputs.archived_copy: The same input bytes are in stage40-ncc-closure/fixtures.tar.gz; input-sha256.json lists them and validation checks the hashes match.

cases.note: 8k is core_only (no refinement, so the hybrid never creates a pose context) on a constant background, as disclosed on 2026-10-19.

methods.shared_settings: Round-40 formal jobs (benchmark_gpu_ncc_closure.job): pose_input_mode 1, pose_storage_mode 1, refinement_backend 1, fine_ncc_mode 2, fine_fused, fine_angle_reuse, stop_layer 1.

arms.frames: Runner source_frames sequence mode, sequence_mode reuse, warmup_seconds 0, source_frames = [the case fixture], repeats = 1 + warmup_calls + measured cycles. Call 0 constructs the Session; every later call decodes the same file again (excluded), then Session::updateSource copies it and releases the hybrid pose context, which the next refinement rebuilds.
arms.static: Round-40 formal job (first call, 1 s time-based warm-up, measured repeats on one unchanged source): same-build control reproducing the round-40 asymmetric scope.
arms.frame_choice: One archived fixture repeated (allowed by the task): content-identical frames keep data-dependent work equal to round 40; this is not a changing camera stream.

schedule.order: per case, per block: hybrid_best_frames, full_gpu_simd_frames, hybrid_best_static, full_gpu_simd_static in even blocks; reversed in odd blocks
schedule.pilot: Same jobs, 1 block, run first after the build (also absorbs first-use Metal shader compilation); screening only, never decision evidence, retained.
schedule.host: No builds, tests or other experiments during timing. The driver refuses a formal start if competing build/benchmark processes exist and records load average, GPU device utilization and competing process names before every worker; any recorded competitor is a retained host_busy gate.

warmup.rule: warmup_calls = max(1, ceil(1500 ms / faster round-40 formal median of the two methods)); planned from stage40-ncc-closure/formal-summary.json
warmup.exclusion: Call 0 (Session construction, cold) and the planned warm-up calls are excluded from every timing distribution and still evaluated against GT.
warmup.gate: elapsed_ms(last warm-up call) - elapsed_ms(call 0) >= 1000 ms in every sequence process, matching the round-40 one-second warm-up; failures retained per block.

metrics.primary: frame_wall_ms of measured calls: Session::updateSource (validation, copy, pose release) plus run; excludes image decode, output comparison and JSON.
metrics.static_control: total_ms of measured repeats, first-call pose_create_ms, measured pose_create_ms (must be 0 for the hybrid)
metrics.memory: Per-process peak RSS and per-call current RSS; named Metal bytes (full GPU gpu_bytes; hybrid frame coarse+fine and pose-context buffers separately). RSS and Metal bytes are never added.

accuracy.scope: Independent GT in the parent process on every cold, warm-up and measured call of the frames arms and every first/measured call of the static arms; static warm-ups have native exactness only.
accuracy.separate_output_checks: Exact ordered matches and proposals across all calls of an arm, and between each frames arm and the same method's static control.

gates: route_and_residency (full GPU: one command buffer, one wait, no intermediate readback, peak1/fine4; hybrid: Metal refinement route)

sequence_route (call 0 constructs; later calls copy w*h bytes, keep the template models, bump the source generation; every refining hybrid call has pose_create_ms > 0 and an invalidated pose; full GPU and core-only calls never create one; runner drained)
static_route (hybrid measured repeats reuse the first-call pose context: pose_create_ms = 0)
time_budget (per block, full GPU frames <= hybrid frames + max(2 ms, 10%), round-40 tolerance)
rss_budget (full GPU frames peak RSS <= hybrid frames + max(8 MiB, 10%))

decision_rules.faster_per_frame: Name a method faster at a case only if the pooled measured median of frame_wall_ms favours it AND all six paired block medians agree in sign; otherwise report the medians and state that the direction is not established.
decision_rules.also_reported: The same rule on total_ms (frames), on the static control (round-40 scope), the per-method reuse effect (frames minus static), and the round-40 estimate method applied to this build's static control.
decision_rules.estimate_held: The archive-only round-40 estimate (fine4 vs hybrid plus first-call pose_create_ms: 128 -4.4%, 512 +15.3%, controlled6 +14.1%, 8K -74.8%) is judged on direction only: held if the measured per-frame direction is established and has the same sign, not held if established with the opposite sign, inconclusive otherwise. The point difference is reported, not gated.
decision_rules.no_adoption_change: Measurement only; GUI and core defaults are not changed.

limits: Single Apple M4 Pro (48 GiB) Metal device
Repeated identical frame; no changing-content camera sequence or real-video accuracy
Sequence RSS includes per-call decoding and the runner retaining all output rows
Cross-round numbers come from different builds and are compared only as an estimate check, never multiplied
